name: Probability of an event
definition: Measures how likely an event A is, from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain). For equally likely outcomes it is the ratio of favorable to total outcomes.

examples.explanation: One face in six on a fair die.

name: Conditional probability
definition: The probability of A given that B occurred: restrict attention to B's outcomes and measure A's share. Bayes' theorem reverses the conditioning.

sources.label: OpenStax Introductory Statistics
sources.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (openstax.org footer); consulted as reference, original wording, no text reused

name: Random variable
definition: A variable whose value is the outcome of chance. Uppercase X names the variable; lowercase x names an observed value. Its distribution lists each value's probability.

examples.explanation: The die-roll variable equals six with probability one sixth.

sources.label: OpenStax Introductory Statistics
sources.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (openstax.org footer); consulted as reference, original wording, no text reused

name: Expected value
definition: The long-run average of a random variable: each value weighted by its probability. For a population it is denoted μ.

sources.label: OpenStax Introductory Statistics
sources.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (openstax.org footer); consulted as reference, original wording, no text reused

name: Population mean
definition: The mean of an entire population, as opposed to a sample mean x̄. It is a fixed (usually unknown) parameter that samples estimate.

examples.explanation: The population mean is the expected value.

sources.label: OpenStax Introductory Statistics
sources.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (openstax.org footer); consulted as reference, original wording, no text reused

name: Variance
definition: Measures spread as the average squared distance from the mean: E[(X − μ)²]. Squaring keeps units squared; the standard deviation restores original units.

examples.explanation: Mean of squares minus square of the mean.

sources.label: OpenStax Introductory Statistics
sources.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (openstax.org footer); consulted as reference, original wording, no text reused

name: Standard deviation
definition: The square root of variance: typical distance from the mean in original units. σ denotes the population value; s denotes a sample's. About 68-95-99.7% of normal data falls within 1-2-3 standard deviations.

examples.explanation: Root of variance restores the original units.

contexts.meaning: σ is the fixed population standard deviation.
s estimates σ from observed data.

sources.label: OpenStax Introductory Statistics
sources.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (openstax.org footer); consulted as reference, original wording, no text reused

name: Covariance
definition: Measures how two variables move together: positive when both run above or below their means simultaneously, negative when they oppose. Its size depends on units, so correlation standardizes it.

sources.label: OpenStax Introductory Statistics
sources.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (openstax.org footer); consulted as reference, original wording, no text reused

name: Correlation
definition: Standardized covariance between −1 and 1. ρ denotes the population value, r the sample value. Near ±1 means a tight linear relationship; near 0 means little linear link (other patterns may exist).

examples.explanation: A strong positive linear association in the sample.

commonMistakes: Reading correlation as causation; it measures linear association only.

sources.label: OpenStax Introductory Statistics
sources.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (openstax.org footer); consulted as reference, original wording, no text reused

name: Normal distribution
definition: The bell-shaped distribution set by its mean μ and variance σ². Sums and averages of many small effects are approximately normal (central limit theorem); the standard normal N(0,1) is the tabulated reference.

examples.explanation: X follows the standard normal distribution.

sources.label: OpenStax Introductory Statistics
sources.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (openstax.org footer); consulted as reference, original wording, no text reused

notes: Convention split: probability theory usually writes N(mu, sigma-squared) with the variance, while some textbooks (including OpenStax) write N(mu, sigma) with the standard deviation. Check which the local text uses.

name: Binomial and Poisson distributions
definition: Models for counts: Bin(n,p) counts successes in n trials with success chance p; Poisson(λ) counts events in a fixed window at rate λ. The chi-squared (χ²) distribution separately models sums of squared normals in tests.

examples.explanation: Choose the successful trials, then weight by chance.

sources.label: OpenStax Introductory Statistics
sources.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (openstax.org footer); consulted as reference, original wording, no text reused

name: z-score
definition: Counts how many standard deviations a value sits from the mean: z = (x − μ)/σ. It puts different datasets on one scale for normal tables and tests.

examples.explanation: Seventy sits two standard deviations above the mean.

sources.label: OpenStax Introductory Statistics
sources.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (openstax.org footer); consulted as reference, original wording, no text reused

name: Sample mean
definition: Averages observed values to estimate the population mean μ. It varies from sample to sample; larger samples cluster tighter around μ.

examples.explanation: Add the observations, divide by how many there are.

sources.label: OpenStax Introductory Statistics
sources.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (openstax.org footer); consulted as reference, original wording, no text reused

name: Sample proportion
definition: The fraction of successes in a sample, estimating the population proportion p. The hat marks it as computed from data.

examples.explanation: Sixty successes in a hundred trials.

sources.label: OpenStax Introductory Statistics
sources.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (openstax.org footer); consulted as reference, original wording, no text reused

name: Estimator (hat notation)
definition: A hat marks an estimate computed from data: θ̂ estimates the unknown parameter θ. Good estimators center on the target (unbiased) and tighten with more data.

examples.explanation: The sample mean estimates the population mean.

sources.label: OpenStax Introductory Statistics
sources.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (openstax.org footer); consulted as reference, original wording, no text reused

name: Null and alternative hypotheses
definition: Frames a test: H₀ states the default (no effect), H₁ the claim under investigation. Evidence against H₀ is measured by the p-value at a preset significance level α.

examples.explanation: Testing whether a mean is positive.

sources.label: OpenStax Introductory Statistics
sources.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (openstax.org footer); consulted as reference, original wording, no text reused

name: p-value
definition: The chance of data this extreme if the null hypothesis held. A small p-value (below α, often 0.05) counts as evidence against H₀; it is not the chance H₀ is true.
commonMistakes: Reading p as the probability the null is true; it assumes the null.

sources.label: OpenStax Introductory Statistics
sources.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (openstax.org footer); consulted as reference, original wording, no text reused

name: Regression prediction (y-hat)
definition: The value a regression line predicts at a given x. Residuals (observed minus predicted) diagnose the fit; the least-squares line minimizes their squares.
